affectedPublicSurfaces: The entire authenticated `/v1/*` API is the SUBJECT of this slice, but no runtime code changes: the deliverable is a generated cross-tenant probe suite (tests only) that reads the committed surface inventory from #1331 (`docs/security/surface_inventory.json`, itself generated from the live route table) and, for every `/v1/*` route that takes a tenant-scoped id, seeds tenants A and B on real Postgres, authenticates as A, requests B's id, and asserts 404 — never 403 (an existence oracle: it confirms the id is real, the reconnaissance step before anything else), never 200.

The 404-indistinguishability contract: for every probed route, the nonexistent-id response must be byte-identical to the cross-tenant response, so the two cases cannot be told apart by a caller. This hardens the contract W6's parent scope already requires (404-not-403 for cross-tenant and nonexistent), so the two in-flight waves agree by construction.

Coverage completeness as a control: the probe covers every method each id-taking route exposes (a read-protected route with an open POST is the defect class this suite exists to find), asserts covered-route count equals id-taking-route count so nothing is skipped by omission, and FAILS THE BUILD on any route the generator cannot classify — unclassifiable is a red build, never a skip.
CI wiring: the probe runs as part of the existing integration job with a stated runtime budget, so a route added next month is covered by default rather than by someone remembering.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Not applicable to the running host — this slice ships tests, not runtime code. The probe runs in CI against the same commit the candidate serves: two tenants seeded on the CI Postgres service, requests driven through the app's own route table in-process. No live host interaction, no production or sandbox credential is resolved, and no vendor call is made at any point.
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: The verification IS the CI run: the probe is generated from #1331's committed inventory (byte-equal to the live route table by #1331's own gate), so a green probe on the merge commit is exactly the claim this slice makes about the deployed API. syntheticShopRequired is TRUE in the CI sense — tenants A and B are seeded synthetic shops on the CI Postgres service; no real merchant's shop or data is touched. If the probe finds a real defect on an existing route (a 403, a 200, or a distinguishable 404 body), that defect is FILED AND FIXED IN ITS OWN ISSUE with its own release evidence — it is never folded into this slice, and the probe is never weakened to keep the build green.

journeys.name: cross-tenant-probe-generated-and-denying
assertions: pre-merge: the probe's cases are generated from #1331's committed inventory (which #1331's own gate holds byte-equal to the live route table) — no hand-written route list exists anywhere in the suite
pre-merge: the count of probed routes is asserted equal to the count of id-taking routes in the inventory, so omission is a test failure rather than silence
pre-merge: for every id-taking route and every method it exposes, authenticated-as-A requesting B's id returns 404 — never 403, never 200 — on real Postgres with two seeded tenants
pre-merge: for every probed route, the nonexistent-id 404 body is byte-identical to the cross-tenant 404 body
pre-merge: a fixture route added in the test and left unclassified fails the probe, naming the route — proving the generator cannot silently skip
pre-merge: a deliberately-weakened handler (one route patched test-locally to return 403) makes its case FAIL — proving the probe asserts what it claims
pre-merge: the unauthenticated allowlist is imported from #1331's single source, not redefined — one allowlist in the repo, asserted by the suite
pre-merge: the probe completes inside its stated runtime budget in the existing integration job

htmlRoutes: No HTML route, page, bundle, or static asset changes — the diff is a generated pytest suite under tests/ plus any generator helper it needs. No file under apps/ or packages/ is touched.

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration and no schema change. The probe seeds tenants A and B through the existing ORM/fixtures on the CI Postgres service inside test transactions/databases; it leaves no persistent state. If implementation concludes it needs any schema support, that is a scope error — stop and report, per the W7 lock that only Meta assigns migration numbers.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. A red probe before merge is the control doing its job: either the generator or a case is wrong (fix it in this slice), or a real cross-tenant defect exists on a live route (file and fix it in its own issue with its own release evidence — this slice does not carry runtime fixes). Never add an exclusion to get green.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Reverting this slice removes coverage and nothing else — no runtime behaviour changes, so rollback is deleting tests. The visible record of what was lost is the probe suite and its inventory-count assertion. A rollback must never be used to silence a probe failure caused by a runtime defect; the defect outlives the revert.

acceptanceCommands: ruff check backend tests && ruff format --check backend tests
doNotInfer: Cases are GENERATED from #1331's committed inventory (docs/security/surface_inventory.json), never from a hand-written route list. A second list is the decay mode this control exists to prevent.
The covered-route count is asserted equal to the id-taking-route count from the inventory. A route the generator cannot classify FAILS the build, naming the route — it is never skipped.
A 403 anywhere in the probe is a FAILURE, not a pass: 403 is an existence oracle. 404 only, and the cross-tenant body must be byte-identical to the nonexistent body.

NO EXCLUSIONS may be added to keep the build green. A W6 route failing the probe is a real defect: REPORT it against the owning W6 issue; do not edit any W6-owned file (apps/**, packages/**, api/routes/demo_decisions.py, services/agent/approval.py, services/agent/runner/core.py, services/agent/sanitize/** source, core/security/dependencies.py) and do not exclude the route.
The unauthenticated allowlist is REUSED from #1331's single source — never redefined. Two allowlists is one too many.
The deliberately-weakened-handler check (a test-local 403 patch making its case fail) is part of the deliverable, not optional hardening.
Tenant-isolation claims run on real Postgres with two seeded tenants — never SQLite (it cannot express the claim), never a single-tenant shortcut.
A real defect found by the probe on an existing route is filed and fixed in its OWN issue with its own release evidence — never folded into this slice, and never 'fixed' by weakening the probe.
This slice ships tests only: no runtime code, no migration, no CI-workflow needs-block rewrites (appends only, per the W7 lock).
